headline: Noise ordinance survey questions approved for public distribution after final edits
summary: The noise survey asks what types of noise bother residents, when it bothers them most, and whether they have reported it to the city. The website survey asks how often people use the site, what they use it for, and whether they use a phone or computer. Both surveys go to the public once final edits are made. Members also approved the City Council newsletter and the neighborhood ward meeting schedule.
decisions: Approved the City Council newsletter for this month, keeping the paper in committee.
Approved the neighborhood ward meeting schedule, 5 in favor.
Approved noise ordinance survey questions for public distribution after final edits, 5-0.
Approved city website survey questions for public distribution after final edits, 5-0.
discussion: Noise survey questions: Members suggested asking police and code enforcement for past complaint records. A resident said Route 93 has caused noise on the east side for 66 years and asked for a sound barrier.

Ward meeting childcare: Members looked into childcare at ward meetings, and the recreation department might bring a counselor with games and crafts. A call to the recreation department will check whether it fits the budget, which may be tight.

Website survey: Members discussed getting site statistics from the IT department and a web design project with vocational school students. IT could provide data on phone and computer use and page visits, and the superintendent could be contacted about students.
